claim: In the case of the TUS conditions, fMRI data collection began only after completion of the TUS train.
source: In the case of the TUS conditions, fMRI data collection began only after completion of the TUS train.

claim: Anaesthesia was induced using intramuscular injection of ketamine (10 mg/kg), xylazine (0.125–0.25 mg/kg), and midazolam (0.1 mg/kg).
source: Anaesthesia was induced using intramuscular injection of ketamine (10 mg/kg), xylazine (0.125–0.25 mg/kg), and midazolam (0.1 mg/kg).

claim: Macaques also received injections of atropine (0.05 mg/kg, intramuscularly), meloxicam (0.2 mg/kg, intravenously), and ranitidine (0.05 mg/kg, intravenously).
source: Macaques also received injections of atropine (0.05 mg/kg, intramuscularly), meloxicam (0.2 mg/kg, intravenously), and ranitidine (0.05 mg/kg, intravenously).

claim: The anaesthetized animals were placed in an MRI-compatible frame in a sphinx position and placed in a horizontal 3 T MRI scanner with a full-size bore.
source: The anaesthetized animals were placed in an MRI-compatible frame (Crist Instruments) in a sphinx position and placed in a horizontal 3 T MRI scanner with a full-size bore.

claim: Scanning commenced ~2 hr after induction, when the clinical peak of ketamine had passed.
source: Scanning commenced ~2 hr after induction, when the clinical peak of ketamine had passed.
evidence: Timing of scan relative to anaesthesia induction.

claim: Anaesthesia was maintained using the lowest possible concentration of isoflurane to ensure that macaques were anaesthetized.
source: Anaesthesia was maintained, in accordance with veterinary recommendation, using the lowest possible concentration of isoflurane to ensure that macaques were anaesthetized.

claim: During the acquisition of the functional data the expired isoflurane concentration was in the range 0.6–0.8%.
source: During the acquisition of the functional data the expired isoflurane concentration was in the range 0.6–0.8%.

claim: Isoflurane was selected for the scans as it was previously demonstrated to preserve rs-fMRI networks.
source: Isoflurane was selected for the scans as it was previously demonstrated to preserve rs-fMRI networks (Mars et al., 2013; Mars et al., 2011; Neubert et al., 2015; Neubert et al., 2014; O'Reilly et al., 2013; Sallet et al., 2013; Vincent et al., 2007).
evidence: Justification for anaesthetic choice with citations.

claim: Macaques were maintained with intermittent positive pressure ventilation to ensure a constant respiration rate during the functional scan.
source: Macaques were maintained with intermittent positive pressure ventilation to ensure a constant respiration rate during the functional scan, and respiration rate, inspired and expired CO2, and inspired and expired isoflurane concentration were monitored and recorded using VitalMonitor software (Vetronic Services Ltd.).
evidence: Description of respiratory support and monitoring.

claim: Core temperature and SpO2 were constantly monitored throughout the scan.
source: Core temperature and SpO2 were also constantly monitored throughout the scan.

claim: A four-channel phased-array coil was used for data acquisition.
source: A four-channel phased-array coil was used for data acquisition (Dr. H. Kolster, Windmiller Kolster Scientific, Fresno, CA, USA).

claim: FMRI data were collected in experiments 1–3 with whole-brain BOLD fMRI data collected for 3 runs of approximately 26 min each.
source: FMRI data were collected in experiments 1–3. In each session whole-brain BOLD fMRI data were collectedfor 3 runs of approximately 26 min each, using the following parameters: 36 axial slices; in-plane resolution, 2 × 2 mm; slice thickness, 2 mm; no slice gap; TR, 2000 ms; TE, 19 ms; 800 volumes per run.

claim: A minimum period of 10 days elapsed between sessions.
source: A minimum period of 10 days elapsed between sessions.

claim: T1-weighted structural MRI scans were collected in experiments 1–3 with a structural scan acquired for each macaque in the same session.
source: T1-weighted structural MRI scans were collected in experiments 1–3. A structural scan (average over up to three T1w images acquired in the same session) was acquired for each macaque in the same session, using a T1 weighted magnetization-prepared rapid-acquisition gradient echo sequence (0.5 × 0.5×0.5 mm voxel resolution).

claim: The pre-processing and analysis of the MRI data was designed to follow the HCP Minimal Processing Pipeline.
source: The pre-processing and analysis of the MRI data was designed to follow the HCP Minimal Processing Pipeline (Glasser et al., 2013), using tools of FSL (https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/fslwiki; RRID:SCR_002823), HCP Workbench (https://www.humanconnectome.org/software/connectome-workbench; RRID:SCR_008750), and the Magnetic Resonance Comparative Anatomy Toolbox (MrCat; https://github.com/neuroecology/MrCat; copy archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/MrCat; Verhagen, 2019).
evidence: Description of analysis pipeline with citations and software references.

claim: The first 5 volumes of the functional EPI datasets were discarded to ensure a steady RF excitation state.
source: The first 5 volumes of the functional EPI datasets were discarded to ensure a steady RF excitation state.

claim: EPI timeseries were motion corrected using MCFLIRT.
source: EPI timeseries were motion corrected using MCFLIRT.

claim: Given that the animals were anaesthetized and their heads were held in a steady position, any apparent image motion is caused by changes to the B0 field and temperature, rather than by head motion.
source: Given that the animals were anaesthetized and their heads were held in a steady position, any apparent image motion, if present at all, is caused by changes to the B0 field and temperature, rather than by head motion.
evidence: Interpretation of motion parameters in anaesthetized subjects.

claim: The parameter estimates from MCFLIRT can be considered to be 'B0-confound parameters' instead of motion parameters.
source: Accordingly, the parameter estimates from MCFLIRT can be considered to be 'B0-confound parameters' instead.

claim: Each timeseries was checked rigorously for spikes and other artefacts, both visually and using automated algorithms.
source: Each timeseries was checked rigorously for spikes and other artefacts, both visually and using automated algorithms; where applicable slices with spikes were linearly interpolated based on temporally neighbouring slices.

claim: The functional timeseries were high-pass filtered with a frequency cut-off at 2000 s.
source: The functional timeseries were high-pass filtered with a frequency cut-off at 2000 s.

claim: Temporally cyclical noise was removed using band-stop filters set dynamically to noise peaks in the frequency domain of the first three principal components of the timeseries.
source: Temporally cyclical noise, for example originating from the respiration apparatus, was removed using band-stop filters set dynamically to noise peaks in the frequency domain of the first three principal components of the timeseries.

claim: To account for remaining global signal confounds, the signal timeseries in white matter (WM) and meningeal compartments were considered.
source: To account for remaining global signal confounds we considered the signal timeseries in white matter (WM) and meningeal compartments.

claim: The WM + meningeal confound timeseries was described by the mean time course and the first five subsequent principal components of the combined WM and meningeal compartment.
source: Specifically, the WM + meningeal confound timeseries was described by the mean time course and the first five subsequent principal components of the combined WM and meningeal compartment (considering only voxels with a high posterior probability of belonging to the WM or meningeal compartment, obtained in the T1w image using FAST).

claim: The B0 confound parameter estimates obtained from MCFLIRT were expanded as a second degree Volterra series to capture both linear and non-linear B0 effects.
source: The B0 confound parameter estimates obtained from MCFLIRT were expanded as a second degree Volterra series to capture both linear and non-linear B0 effects.

claim: The WM + meningeal and expanded B0 confound parameters were regressed out of the BOLD signal for each voxel.
source: Together the WM + meningeal and expanded B0 confound parameters were regressed out of the BOLD signal for each voxel.

claim: In a separate analysis to assess the contribution of the meningeal compartment signal, the procedure was repeated with the mean and principal components extracted from signal in the WM compartment alone, excluding the meningeal compartment.
source: In a separate analysis (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1), to assess the contribution of the meningeal compartment signal we repeated the identical procedure as above, with the only difference that the mean and principal components were extracted from signal in the WM compartment alone, excluding the meningeal compartment.

claim: Following the confound cleaning step, the timeseries were low-pass filtered with a cut-off at 10 s.
source: Following this confound cleaning step, the timeseries were low-pass filtered with a cut-off at 10 s.

claim: The cleaned and filtered signal was projected from the volumetric representation to the F99 cortical surface, while maintaining the subcortical volumetric structures.
source: The cleaned and filtered signal was projected from the conventional volumetric representation (2 mm voxels) to the F99 cortical surface (~1.4 mm spaced vertices), while maintaining the subcortical volumetric structures.

claim: The data were spatially smoothed using a 3 mm FWHM gaussian kernel, while considering the folding of the cortex and the anatomical boundaries of the subcortical structures.
source: The data were spatially smoothed using a 3 mm FWHM gaussian kernel, while considering the folding of the cortex and the anatomical boundaries of the subcortical structures.

claim: The data timeseries were demeaned to prepare for functional connectivity analyses.
source: Lastly, the data timeseries were demeaned to prepare for functional connectivity analyses.

claim: To represent group effects the run-concatenated timeseries of all animals were combined using a group-PCA approach resulting in a series of 200 volumes representing the principal components.
source: To represent group effects the run-concatenated timeseries of all animals were combined using a group-PCA approach resulting in a series of 200 volumes representing the principal components (Smith et al., 2014).
evidence: Description of group-level analysis approach with citation.

claim: Fingerprint target regions were drawn from the literature and chosen based on their known and distinct connectivity, either strong or weak, with the seed region.
source: Fingerprint target regions were drawn from the literature and chosen based on their known and distinct connectivity, either strong or weak, with the seed region.

claim: To construct regions-of-interest (ROI) for SMA and FPC, circles of 4 mm radius were drawn on the cortical surface around the point closest to the average stimulation coordinate in both hemispheres.
source: To construct regions-of-interest (ROI) for SMA and FPC, circles of 4 mm radius were drawn on the cortical surface around the point closest to the average stimulation coordinate (Figure 2), in both the left and the right hemisphere.

claim: Coupling between the activity of each region of interest and the rest of the brain was estimated by calculating the correlation coefficient between each point in the ROI and all other data points.
source: Coupling between the activity of each region of interest and the rest of the brain was estimated by calculating the correlation coefficient between each point in the ROI and all other data points (Fisher's z: inverse hyperbolic tangent of Pearson's r, bounded at [−2 2]).

claim: The resulting 'connectivity-maps' were averaged across all vertices/voxels in the ROI, and subsequently averaged across hemispheres.
source: The resulting 'connectivity-maps' were averaged across all vertices/voxels in the ROI, and subsequently averaged across hemispheres.

claim: The final maps represent the average coupling of a bilateral ROI with the rest of the brain.
source: Accordingly, the final maps represent the average coupling of a bilateral ROI with the rest of the brain.

claim: The fingerprints are obtained by extracting the average coupling with each target ROI and averaging across the two hemispheres.
source: The fingerprints are obtained by extracting the average coupling with each target ROI and averaging across the two hemispheres.

claim: All suitable animals available at the time of experimentation took part in this study.
source: All suitable animals available at the time of experimentation took part in this study. Accordingly, there was no pre-selection nor restriction for group allocation.

claim: No data was excluded for analysis.
source: No data was excluded for analysis.

claim: Sample sizes could not be predetermined statistically in the absence of a prior literature reporting relevant expected effect sizes.
source: Sample sizes could not be predetermined statistically in the absence of a prior literature reporting relevant expected effect sizes; instead we adopted sample sizes similar to those reported in previous publications detailing (interventional) macaque fMRI studies (Chau et al., 2015; O'Reilly et al., 2013; Papageorgiou et al., 2017).
evidence: Justification for sample size with citations.

claim: Data collection and analysis were not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.
source: Data collection and analysis were not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.

claim: A group PCA approach was used to define the centre of group rs-fMRI effects.
source: We used a group PCA approach to define the centre of group rs-fMRI effects (see Macaque rs-fMRI analyses).

claim: For all other effects the centre of the group is defined as the mean of the individual subject effects.
source: For all other effects the centre of the group is defined as the mean of the individual subject effects.

claim: Non-parametric permutation tests were performed on cosine similarity metrics summarizing pairs of fingerprints.
source: Importantly, rather than examining activity coupling between the seed area and each of the fingerprint ROIs in turn and risking potential false positive results, we compared the overall pattern of coupling using the method devised by Mars and colleagues (Mars et al., 2016); non-parametric permutation tests were performed on cosine similarity metrics summarizing pairs of fingerprints (SMA TUS versus control and FPC TUS versus control).
evidence: Description of statistical approach with citation.

claim: Each connectional fingerprint can be represented as a multidimensional vector, with the number of dimensions corresponding to the number of target ROIs in the fingerprint.
source: Each connectional fingerprint can be represented as a multidimensional vector, with the number of dimensions corresponding to the number of target ROIs in the fingerprint.

claim: The cosine similarity metric quantifies the angle between two multi-dimensional vectors and takes into account the shape of the fingerprint irrespective of its mean amplitude.
source: The cosine similarity metric quantifies the angle between two of such multi-dimensional vectors. As such, it takes into account the shape of the fingerprint irrespective of its mean amplitude and results in a single metric per pair of fingerprints, negating the necessity for correcting for multiple comparisons across fingerprint targets.
evidence: Description of cosine similarity metric properties.

claim: The relatively small number of TUS sites, animals, and fMRI runs allowed exhaustive testing of all possible permutations (24309) to obtain the true probability of rejecting the null hypothesis.
source: The relatively small number of TUS sites, animals, and fMRI runs allowed us to exhaustively test all possible permutations (24309) to obtain the true probability of rejecting the null hypothesis.

claim: All other statistical inferences were drawn in the context of generalized linear mixed-effects (GLME) models that considered the intercept and factorial design as fixed effects and the intercept and slope grouped per animal as random effects.
source: All other statistical inferences were drawn in the context of generalized linear mixed-effects (GLME) models that considered the intercept and factorial design (including interactions where appropriate) as fixed effects and the intercept and slope grouped per animal as random effects with possible correlation between them (as implemented in MATLAB, Mathworks, Natick, USA).

claim: The models were assumed to adhere to a normal distribution of the data and were fitted using Maximum-Pseudo-Likelihood estimation methods.
source: The models were assumed to adhere to a normal distribution of the data (not formally tested) and were fitted using Maximum-Pseudo-Likelihood estimation methods where the covariance of the random effects was approximated using Cholesky parameterization.
evidence: Description of model assumptions and fitting.

claim: Statistical significance was set at α = 0.05, two-tailed.
source: Statistical significance was set at α = 0.05, two-tailed, and estimated using conventional analyses of variance (ANOVA).

claim: Prior to histological examination, animals were anaesthetized with sodium pentorbarbitone and perfused with 90% saline and 10% formalin.
source: In experiment 4, prior to histological examination, animals were anaesthetized with sodium pentorbarbitone and perfused with 90% saline and 10% formalin.

claim: A post-mortem examination of the surface of the brain was conducted prior to the brain extraction.
source: A post-mortem examination of the surface of the brain was conducted prior to the brain extraction.

claim: The brains were removed and placed in 10% sucrose formalin.
source: The brains were then removed and placed in 10% sucrose formalin.

claim: The brains were blocked in the coronal plane at the level of the lunate sulcus.
source: The brains were blocked in the coronal plane at the level of the lunate sulcus.

claim: Each brain was cut in 50 μm coronal sections.
source: Each brain was cut in 50 μm coronal sections.

claim: Every tenth section, two adjacent sections were retained for analysis whereby one was stained with Cresyl Violet (Nissl body staining) and the other with Haemotoxylin and Eosin (H and E staining).
source: Every tenth section, two adjacent sections were retained for analysis whereby one was stained with Cresyl Violet (Nissl body staining) and the other with Haemotoxylin and Eosin (H and E staining), in line with previous studies (Dallapiazza et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2016b).
evidence: Description of histological staining with citations.
